title: Microkernel fusion for precision-transition + decode-prefetch windowing
creator: Alex Chen
description:
Goal: implement and validate a set of microkernel fusions and a lightweight decode-prefetch windowing heuristic that minimize dequantization overhead in mixed-precision (INT8/FP8) serving paths while preserving model quality and latency SLOs.

Context: Current mixed-precision paths frequently materialize dequantized tensors early in the pipeline which increases GPU memory traffic and adds extra kernels (cast/copy/transpose) during prefill and streaming decode. We want a runtime approach that: 1) defers dequantization until absolutely necessary, 2) fuses cast+transpose+matmul micro-ops where beneficial, and 3) schedules prefill/decode batches using a small prefetch window to warm KV caches without violating latency SLOs.

Scope: prototype new microkernels for asymmetric INT8->FP16 transitions, headwise scale fusion for attention q/k/v, zero-copy view-based cast lanes for streaming decode, and a prefill-prefetch scheduler that decides a conservative window size per-model based on tokenizer distribution and recent sequence-length histograms. This ticket includes design, implementation of fused kernels in the runtime, end-to-end perf benchmarks, and a staged rollout with telemetry gating.

Non-goals: full quantization-aware retraining or offline calibration tooling (separate initiative), wholesale model format changes.

Key design ideas:
- Precision-transition trampolines: runtime micro-paths that delay materializing FP tensors by using fused microkernels that accept INT8 inputs and internally apply dequant scaling combined with matrix multiplication (INT8->FP32 accumulation where hardware requires). This reduces memory writes and kernel launches.
- Headwise fused QKV loader: combine dequant, head-splitting, and layout transpose into a single microkernel to cut prefill overhead on wide models with many heads.
- Asymmetric quant-friendly attention: kernels that support per-head scale/zero-point and avoid global requant step when downstream can consume mixed precision.
- Decode-prefetch windowing: heuristic that issues 1..N speculative prefill requests for likely next tokens during streaming generation to warm KV cache. Window N is model- and workload-configurable and bounded to keep tail latency within SLOs.
- Zero-copy cast lanes: use view semantics and kernel-level casting where possible to avoid copies; fallback to temporary buffers only when required by accelerator primitives.

Trade-offs and acceptance criteria (see below) reflect accuracy vs perf balance; we will prioritize conservative defaults that prefer correctness.

Data & telemetry required:
- Microbenchmark traces: per-kernel time, memory traffic, kernel launch count.
- End-to-end p95/p99 latency on representative prompts and streaming workloads.
- Quality metrics: perplexity/regression on small eval prompt set and token-level divergence tests.
- Failure telemetry to detect correctness/overflow in fused dequant paths.

Artifacts & links:
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood/example/microkernel-fusion-2025 (draft)
- Prototype PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289
- Benchmark dashboard (internal): https://dash.redwood/bench/runtime/ENG-99371

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged runtime build with fused kernels disabled by default.
2) Canary on non-critical models with synthetic traffic for 48h.
3) Look for regressions in quality or p99 latency; if stable, enable for broader model family.
4) Add model-specific window configurations to catalog and surface suggestions in Optimize.

Risks:
- Numeric regressions for extreme quant ranges; mitigate with per-head scaling and runtime checks.
- Some accelerators may not provide required accumulation precision; need fallbacks to standard FP path.
- Prefetch windowing could increase request volume; rate-limiting and conservative defaults mitigate this.
acceptance_criteria: Microkernel fusion reduces total kernel launches during prefill by >= 25% on benchmark model A (12B, 2048 seq).
End-to-end p95 latency for streaming decode improves by >= 10% without increasing p99 by more than 5%.
Quality regressions (token divergence / perplexity) are within 0.5% of baseline on the eval set.
No GPU memory OOMs in canary for 95th-percentile prompt length distributions.
Feature gated and telemetry-producing; dashboard surfaced for rollouts.

comments: 2025-02-11 Alex Chen: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded to Confluence. Decided to prototype fused INT8 matmul accumulation first because it yields biggest wins in initial sims.
2025-02-18 Priya Kapoor: Prototype microkernel shows ~28% fewer launches on local NV GPU for 8-token prefill case; p95 improved ~12% but p99 unchanged. Pushing PR for internal review (see PR#1289).
2025-02-22 Maya Rodriguez (ML): Ran eval against 5k prompt set. Small token-level divergence at tail tokens observed (~0.7%). Investigating per-head scaling adjustments to tighten numeric error.
2025-02-27 Infra: Added telemetry counters for kernel_fused_path and prefetch_window_issued; dashboards warming up. Need better labeling per model family.

2025-03-01 Priya Kapoor: Discovered an edge-case when window N > 2 with certain tokenizers producing long continuations -> rate-limiter triggered in gateway. Updated scheduler to cap outstanding speculative prefills per-account.

2025-03-04 Alex Chen: Updated acceptance criteria to allow up to 5% p99 regression temporarily behind a rollout gate; still aiming for no regression post-tuning. Next: finalize fallback logic for accelerators that lack INT8 accumulation support.
